title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: What’s new, what’s in the beta & what’s next
content:
Macworld





macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on September 14, introducing an all-new Siri AI assistant, major updates to Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, and expanded child-safety features. Design refinements and performance improvements round out the release.
Named after California’s iconic Golden Gate, the update continues Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, bringing Apple Intelligence to more parts of the operating system to help users complete everyday tasks faster.
macOS 27 supports all Macs powered by Apple silicon, but drops support for Intel-based models. Intel Macs can continue running older versions of macOS, with security updates expected to remain available for a limited time.
This guide covers macOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible Macs and the latest beta developments. We explain what’s available now, which features are being tested and what’s expected in future updates, including when those additions could arrive.


What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

				
					

				
			
Apple




Here are the top ten new features and changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate.
Siri AI: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
Apple Intelligence: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
Safari upgrades: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
Smarter Messages and Mail: Better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
New Photos tools: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up, and better search and organization.
More powerful built-in apps: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts, and Image Playground.
Expanded parental controls: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
Better Mac gaming: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
Refined Liquid Glass design: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows, and improved iPhone Mirroring.
Faster macOS performance: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.






macOS 27 latest version: What’s in macOS 27.2.1
macOS 27 became available to install on compatible Macs on September 14.
The latest public version is macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, released on November 9, 2026. This security update addresses vulnerabilities affecting Messages, Bluetooth, AirPlay and other system components.
Two Messages vulnerabilities could allow a remote attacker to join an iMessage group conversation and receive its messages, or enable a newly added participant to access messages sent before they joined. Apple has fixed both issues.
The update also addresses Bluetooth vulnerabilities that could allow a malicious nearby device to pair without user interaction or corrupt process memory. AirPlay fixes prevent attackers within Bluetooth range or on the same network from bypassing limits on pairing-code attempts.
Apple hasn’t indicated that these vulnerabilities were actively exploited, but the potential privacy and security implications make this an important update. To install it, open System Settings > General > Software Update.
What was in macOS 27.2?
Apple released macOS 27.2 on October 26, 2026. Alongside bug fixes and security updates, it added:
Better Siri context: Siri can recall earlier conversations and use additional information, including Messages photo attachments, Calendar attendees and voicemails, with improved results from Safari history and Reading List.
Excluded Apps: One setting controls which apps Siri, Search and suggestions can access.
Write with Siri in Mail: Access it from the message-composition formatting bar.
Messages Suggestions: Turn conversation details into actions in Calendar and Reminders.
Shared Albums improvements: Edit captions and comments, avoid duplicate photos and receive expiry reminders.
SynthID support: Identify AI-generated or modified images in Photos and Image Playground.
Podcasts changes: Separate sections for new episodes and unfinished listening.
FaceTime accessibility: Add a third-party sign-language interpreter or live captioner
What was in macOS 27.1?
Apple did not release macOS 27.1. Following macOS 27.0.1, the next public Mac update was macOS 27.2. Apple released iOS 27.1 specifically for the iPhone Duo. 
What was in macOS 27.0.1?
Apple released macOS 27.0.1 on September 28, 2026, with bug fixes following Golden Gate’s launch. It included a fix for Platform Single Sign-on (SSO): username and password fields could fail to appear on the Lock Screen after waking from sleep. 






Latest macOS 27 Beta
Latest developer beta: macOS 27.3 beta, first release November 3, 2026.
Latest public beta: macOS 27.3 public beta, first release November 5, 2026.

				
					

				
			

Apple




Apple released the first macOS 27.3 developer beta on November 3, 2026. The first public beta followed on November 5, opening testing to members of Apple’s Beta Software Program. 
Full Disk Access changes: Apple is tightening the controls around Full Disk Access, a permission that gives apps access to protected data, including files, mail, messages and browsing history. Apple says granting this level of access should require explicit user action, particularly as AI agents become more capable. As detailed in our report on Full Disk Access changes, macOS 27.3 beta testing indicates that users must manually add an app in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access. Previously, an app could add itself to the list, leaving the user to enable its permission. 
New Safari features: The beta update introduces new Safari features, including vertical tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode and additional Siri browser controls. 
iCloud public-link checks: Also in the beta is evidence that Apple will check iCloud content shared using “Anyone with the link” for harmful content. This includes publicly linked photos and files in iCloud Photos and iCloud Drive. Items shared this way are accessible to Apple and are not end-to-end encrypted, even when Advanced Data Protection is enabled. The checks concern public-link sharing, rather than everything you store in iCloud. To restrict access to invited or approved recipients, choose “People you choose” when sharing a link. See Apple’s explanation of public-link sharing.
Live Activities: The macOS 27.3 beta also adds Live Activities from Mac apps, including Music and Clock, along with system functions such as screen recording. These show ongoing activity in the menu bar, so you can check it without bringing the app’s window to the front. Live Activities appear as small oval indicators to the left of the menu-bar icons. Click an indicator to expand it, then click the arrow to collapse it. When several activities are running, their indicators appear alongside one another. You don’t need a touchscreen MacBook Pro or Dynamic Island: the feature is available on other Macs running the macOS 27.3 beta.
Want to run the beta? Here’s how you can participate in the beta program we also recommend reading our guide to whether you should install the latest macOS beta. Beta software can cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain and, in some cases, data loss. If you install a beta, make a full backup first and, ideally, use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.






What features are still to come in macOS 27
At the time of the launch of macOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Some new features arrived in macOS 27.2, but there are still missing features, including:
Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 






macOS 27 problems: Are there any issues with Golden Gate?
Since macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on Macs there have been reports in the Apple Support Community of issues with Mission Control and Spaces. 
These include: 
Stuttering or delayed transitions: Reports long pauses before a new Space appears. 
Black or missing desktop previews: A black screen may appear when switching Spaces. 
French website MacGeneration was able to reproduce some Mission Control glitches. 






Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features  

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is now a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.
Siri AI behaves more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.
At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?
Conversational AI assistant: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.
Dedicated Siri app: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.
Personal context awareness: Siri can understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.
Web-powered answers: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.
App actions and automation: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.
Spotlight integration: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.
Visual Intelligence: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Visual Intelligence initially placed Blutenburg in Denmark.

Macwelt





Writing Tools: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.
Improved dictation: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting.
Custom Siri voices: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.
A Siri AI contextural popover was discovered during beta testing. Selecting text brings up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions, including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. However, the feature is not enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate. It remains unclear whether Apple intends to make it available as a consumer-facing feature. 
Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. In our testing, Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.
Siri AI has launched as a beta, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements.
With macOS 27.2, Siri AI supports French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish in addition to English. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI is available on Mac and Vision Pro in the European Union, although Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone and iPad in the EU at launch because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act. It is also unavailable in mainland China while Apple works through regulatory requirements.
Which Macs support Siri AI?
Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements. Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.




Safari features in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Notify Me in Safari

Apple




Safari gets several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organization, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation, and performance improvements.
Automatic Tab Topics: Safari automatically groups related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organized. These groups can also be saved for later.
Notify Me: Safari can monitor webpages for changes and alert you when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
Describe an Extension: Users can create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari generates the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
Faster, more efficient browsing: Apple says Safari uses less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

				
					

				
			
Get notified. 

Macwelt




Safari features coming in macOS 27.3
The macOS 27.3 beta adds three new Safari features:
Vertical tabs: Open tabs can appear down the left side of the browser window. They initially appear as icons, but you can widen the sidebar to display their titles.
Adaptive Dark Mode: Safari can apply a dark appearance to websites that don’t offer their own dark mode. You can enable it automatically or choose which sites use it.
Siri browser controls: On compatible Macs, Siri can perform tasks such as clearing Safari’s cache and organizing tabs.






Messages and Mail features in macOS 27
Messages and Mail gain deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.
Messages
Suggestions in Messages (added in macOS 27.2): Messages suggests actions based on your conversation, such as creating a Calendar event for dinner plans or adding a reminder.
Smarter Photo Suggestions: Messages surfaces relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
Personalized Smart Reply: During the preview at WWDC Apple indicated that suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging. This was removed from the iOS 27 beta before launch and hasn’t arrived with macOS 27. 
Improved syncing: Messages should sync more reliably across devices, while failed messages automatically retry sending.
Mail
Personalized Smart Reply: Apple also previewed a feature in Mail whereby it could generates suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to, but this is absent from the first version of macOS 27. 
More relevant search: A new ranking system prioritizes the most useful search results, alongside improved search indexing.
Faster and more accurate: Apple says Mail loads messages more quickly and provide more reliable unread counts.






Photos features in macOS 27
Photos has new AI-powered editing and organization tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.
Spatial Reframing: Photos will intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
Extend Tool: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
Enhanced Clean Up: Apple’s Clean Up tool is better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
Better organisation and search: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.
Faster iCloud syncing: iCloud Photos can begin uploads more quickly, with an option to prioritize syncing when needed.






Other new app features in macOS 27
macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.
Passwords
In macOS 27 the Passwords app will automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work. Read: Apple finally got rid of my biggest password headache. 
This feature was not included in the initial macOS 27 release and may arrive in a subsequent update. 
Image Playground
Image Playground gets a substantial AI upgrade, including the ability to create photorealistic images and make more convincing edits to existing pictures, such as changing colours, hair and other details. Apple continues to apply safeguards around real people, copyrighted characters and distinctive artistic styles. macOS 27.2 added SynthID support for images generated or modified using Photos and Image Playground.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Calendar
Calendar gains natural-language event creation, making it possible to describe an event rather than manually entering every detail. It can also make changes to multiple events at once.
Preview
Preview supports more document formats, improves PDF editing and saves PDF files more quickly.
Notes
Notes gains drawing tools for sketching with a mouse or trackpad, along with digital signatures, Markdown copy-and-paste and links to sections within notes.

				
					

				
			
Notes now features a drawing tool as well as the ability to create and use digital signatures.

Foundry




Freeform
Freeform adds drawing tools, collaborative folders and improved organisation, including the ability to sort boards into folders. Full dark-mode support also changes the appearance of the drawing canvas.

				
					

				
			
In Freeform, boards can now be organised into folders.

Foundry




Weather
Weather gets a clearer and more detailed forecast interface, with reorganised information tiles and enhanced 10-day forecasts showing precipitation probability and amount, as well as wind speeds throughout the day.

				
					

				
			
In the Weather app, the tiles have been rearranged, and there are separate 10-day forecasts for precipitation and wind (circled in red).

Foundry




Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains a redesigned editor, more automation capabilities and one of macOS 27’s more ambitious AI features: the ability to turn natural-language instructions into working automations.

				
					

				
			Shortcuts can start automatically when a specific event occurs.

Thomas Armbrüster




Parental Controls
Apple expands its family-safety tools with Safari’s Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time and Time Allowances, contact approvals, and broader Communication Safety protections. The changes give parents more control over what children can access and who they can communicate with without completely locking down the Mac.
The redesigned parental controls also have a family-wide software requirement. To activate them through Family Sharing, every eligible device in the group – not just the parent’s Mac – must be running iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 or visionOS 27.
Once Apple offers the migration, the family organizer or a parent or guardian should see a Get Started prompt in Family settings. Apple says parents can also select the child’s name under System Settings > Family to begin setup, although the migration options are not currently appearing for everyone.
Older devices that cannot install version 27 can continue using the previous Screen Time and Family Sharing controls. Apple says these legacy devices should not prevent supported hardware from using the redesigned system, but it has acknowledged delays and incorrect device-status information affecting some families..
Accessibility, Shared Albums and Suggestions
macOS 27 also includes accessibility improvements, expanded Shared Albums, and more contextual Suggestions throughout the operating system.
Game Porting Toolkit 4
Apple’s Game Porting Toolkit 4 arrives alongside macOS 27 and promises significant improvements for running and porting Windows games on Apple silicon Macs. Early beta testing suggests substantial performance gains. On an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, GTA V reportedly increased from around 106fps to 176fps, while Red Dead Redemption 2 improved from roughly 60fps to 75fps.
The results suggest software compatibility, rather than raw Apple silicon performance, is increasingly the main obstacle to better Mac gaming. Improvements to Game Porting Toolkit could make Windows titles more practical to run and easier for developers to bring to macOS.






Design and Interface Changes in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




macOS 27 Golden Gate refines the Liquid Glass redesign introduced in macOS 26, with Apple focusing on readability, consistency and usability rather than another major visual overhaul.
Changes include:
Improved Liquid Glass: Stronger contrast, better readability and more consistent refraction effects across windows, menus and controls.
Customizable transparency: Users can adjust the Liquid Glass effect in System Settings, from a clearer appearance to a more heavily tinted look.
Cleaner Finder and toolbars: Finder sidebars are more clearly defined, toolbars are more consistent, and edge-to-edge sidebars replace some of the floating elements introduced in macOS 26.
More consistent windows: Window corners, controls and active-window highlighting have been standardized to make the interface feel more coherent.
Updated icons and menus: Menu-bar and app icons gain sharper outlines, improved contrast and more depth, while unnecessary menu icons have been reduced.
Smoother window management: Mission Control and Spaces animations have been refined, and active windows should be easier to distinguish.
New wallpapers and screensavers: Golden Gate-themed backgrounds include animated daytime and nighttime views of the bridge.
Swipe to refresh: Supported Mac apps gain a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture.
Improved iPhone Mirroring: iPhone Mirroring adds Control Center access, resizable app windows and support for DRM-protected video.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Touch on Mac: How macOS works with a touchscreen
macOS 27 supports direct touchscreen input on the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. Touch works alongside the keyboard and trackpad, giving you another way to interact with apps rather than replacing the controls you already use.
You can swipe to scroll through webpages, pinch to zoom into photos, and drag content between documents. Window gestures include double-tapping to fill the screen and flicking a window to tile it into place. Apple says many existing apps work immediately because macOS translates touches into mouse clicks, while developers can use updated gesture APIs to build more specialized touch controls.
Apple has also announced touch-focused updates for creative apps. Examples include playing onscreen instruments in Logic Pro and selecting ranges, placing clips and zooming into edits in Final Cut Pro. These app updates are scheduled for November.
Direct touchscreen input requires compatible hardware: the 14-inch or 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. 






Performance improvements and system changes in macOS 27
Apple says macOS 27 focuses on speed, efficiency and everyday usability, with improvements across apps, networking, displays and system tasks. Most of these changes do not require Apple Intelligence.
Changes include:
Faster overall performance: Apps should launch more quickly, while an optimized CPU scheduler improves system responsiveness.
Faster Spotlight and setup: Spotlight indexing and new user-account creation are quicker.
Faster file transfers and networking: AirDrop and network file browsing are faster, while Ethernet status can appear in the menu bar.
Thunderbolt and Bluetooth improvements: RDMA over Thunderbolt has been improved, alongside more efficient Bluetooth power management.
Faster Safari: The Safari Start Page loads more quickly, with broader browser performance improvements.
Better external-display support: New high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes include 5K at 120Hz, alongside improved display-position persistence, HDR support for the macOS interface and 5K Mac mirroring.
Apple Intelligence powered changes:
AI-powered file naming – requires Apple Intelligence: macOS can suggest filenames and folder names based on their contents, including in Pages, Numbers, TextEdit and Finder.
Systemwide proofreading – requires Apple Intelligence: Apple Intelligence provides automatic proofreading and improved spelling and grammar suggestions throughout macOS.
Apple Intelligence privacy: Apple says AI processing happens on-device where possible, with Private Cloud Compute used for more demanding tasks. Data processed in the cloud is not stored or made accessible to Apple.






macOS 27 Compatible Macs 

				
					

				
			
The MacBook Neo and other Macs in Apple’s current lineup will all be compatible with macOS 27.

Foundry




Apple states that macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with:
MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 2026)
MacBook Air (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
iMac (Apple silicon, 2021 and later)
Mac mini (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
Mac Studio (2022 and later)
Mac Pro (Apple silicon, 2023 and later)
All supported Macs can run Apple Intelligence, although some of the most advanced Siri AI features require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory.
What about Intel Macs?
macOS 27 marks another major step in Apple’s transition away from Intel. macOS 26 Tahoe was the final version to support Intel Macs, and Apple is now encouraging developers to remove Intel code from their apps and focus on Apple silicon.
macOS 27 will also be the final version to support Rosetta, Apple’s translation technology for running Intel-only apps on Apple silicon Macs. Those apps will continue to work in macOS 27, but will stop working in macOS 28 unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions.
To help users prepare, macOS 27 includes an Intel-app checker in System Settings that lists Intel-based apps used during the past year. If you still rely on any essential Intel-only software, now is a good time to look for updates or alternatives before upgrading to macOS 28.
What happens to DVD support?
macOS 27 also begins the phase-out of Apple’s native DVD support. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK and says it will disappear completely in a future version of macOS.
Golden Gate may still include the DVD Player app, but it is likely to be the last macOS release with Apple’s built-in DVD playback support. Users who still watch DVDs on a Mac will increasingly need to rely on third-party software such as VLC.






 FAQ 


1.
When was macOS 27 Golden Gate released?
September 14, 2026.





2.
Should I install macOS 27?
Golden Gate builds on macOS 26 Tahoe rather than reinventing macOS all over again. The biggest changes come from Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, alongside improvements to Safari, Spotlight, Photos, parental controls, and everyday system performance.
But how much has actually changed since macOS 26 Tahoe, and is macOS 27 worth installing? We have a separate article that explains how Golden Gate compares with macOS Tahoe and which Macs will benefit most from upgrading.






3.
Which Macs can run macOS 27?
All M-series Macs can run macOS 27, and the MacBook Neo.
Certain Siri AI features – most powerful on-device model, expressive voices and advanced dictation – are only available for M3 Macs and newer.





4.
Should Intel Mac owners upgrade now?
Intel Mac owners should start planning a move to Apple silicon, particularly if they want macOS 27, Apple Intelligence or continued access to the latest Mac features. The transition away from Intel hardware has reached a critical turning point, with software support rapidly vanishing and a new generation of affordable entry-level hardware making the switch more accessible than ever.
Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 will not support any Intel-based Macs. While a small number of Intel models may receive security patches for older versions of macOS until September 2028, they are already excluded from modern flagship features.
Those with Intel Macs also miss out on many features, including Apple Intelligence.





5.
Will macOS 27 support Rosetta and Intel apps?
macOS 27 will run Intel-only Mac apps through Rosetta 2. However, macOS 27 will be the final version of macOS to support Rosetta 2 as a general-purpose translation technology for running Intel-based Mac apps on Apple silicon.
Rosetta has acted as a transition layer since Apple introduced its own Mac chips in 2020, translating x86_64 Intel instructions so older software can run on Apple silicon. After macOS 27, most Intel-only Mac apps will no longer work unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions, although Apple will retain limited Rosetta functionality for some older, unmaintained games.
Apple is already preparing users for the change. Since macOS 26.4, Macs can display warnings when launching apps that rely on Rosetta, encouraging users (and the app developers) to update to Apple silicon-native versions before general Rosetta support ends.
In macOS 28, most Intel-only apps will no longer run unless developers update them for Apple silicon.





6.
When is macOS usually updated?
Here is a history of release dates for macOS:
macOS 27 Golden Gate: September 14, 2026
macOS 26 Tahoe: September 15, 2025
macOS 15 Sequoia: September 16, 2024
macOS 14 Sonoma: September 26, 2023
macOS 13 Ventura: October 25, 2022
macOS 12 Monterey: October 25, 2021
macOS 11 Big Sur: November 19, 2020
macOS 10.15 Catalina: October 7, 2019
macOS 10.14 Mojave: September 24, 2018
macOS 10.13 High Sierra: September 25, 2017
macOS 10.12 Sierra: September 20, 2016

title: iPhone 20 Pro: Ten Big Changes That Could Redefine Apple's Flagship
content:
In 2017, Apple celebrated the iPhone's 10th birthday with the iPhone X, the biggest redesign in the product's history. For the device's 20th anniversary, all the rumors indicate that the company is preparing another landmark redesign.


The commemorative "iPhone 20" model isn't expected until September 2027, but leaks have been piling up for months. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple is already deep into its development, and the picture forming across multiple reports is of an iPhone that looks like a single, uninterrupted slab of glass. Here's what we're expecting:

A quad-curved, all-glass design: The display glass reportedly curves away on all four sides, concealing the metal frame during normal use. Apple is said to be working with Samsung on an "equal-depth quad-curved" display to achieve the effect.

Advanced OLED technology: Apple was reportedly planning a brighter, thinner Samsung OLED panel using Color Filter on Encapsulation (COE) for the anniversary iPhone, but a more recent report suggests the technology has slipped: UBI Research does not expect COE on Apple's Pro iPhones until 2029, casting doubt on its inclusion in the 2027 model.

Under-display Face ID and camera: Apple is reportedly continuing to test hardware that would eliminate the final visible cutout from the front of the device. Apple already debuted an under-display camera on the iPhone Duo's inner screen, but reviewers criticized its image quality. Whether an improved version will be ready for the iPhone 20's rumored fall 2027 launch remains uncertain.

Solid-state buttons: Apple is said to be testing haptic replacements for the Side, Volume, Action, and Camera Control buttons. The buttons could be integrated directly into the device's frame, with no actual physical movement when pressed, yet retaining a tactile responsiveness.

Apple modem in the United States: Apple is developing modems that it hopes will outperform Qualcomm's on speed and AI functionality; its third-generation modem, due in 2027, is the one expected to finally exceed Qualcomm's. The C1 and C1X are used in the iPhone 16e and iPhone Air, and the C2 now powers the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Only the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max still uses a Qualcomm modem.

Custom Apple image sensor: Apple is said to be developing its own stacked image sensor to replace the Sony sensors it has traditionally used for the iPhone. Apple has reportedly already developed a working prototype. The sensor is said to use LOFIC technology, which would let each pixel store varying amounts of light and potentially reach up to 20 stops of dynamic range.

A 2-nanometer A21 chip: The 20th anniversary models are expected to feature a second-generation 2-nanometer chip. Following the A20 Pro in this year's iPhone 18 Pro models, the anniversary models would likely be powered by the A21 Pro.

Silicon anode battery: Apple is reportedly exploring a new battery technology that uses a silicon anode capable of storing more lithium ions per gram, potentially delivering longer battery life without increasing the physical size of the battery.

Mobile high bandwidth memory: Apple is rumored to be evaluating vertically stacked DRAM technology to improve memory bandwidth and boost on-device AI performance.

Two sizes: The two anniversary models are expected to be slightly larger than the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, with Digital Chat Station claiming 6.41-inch and 6.96-inch displays, the larger of which would likely be marketed as a 7-inch panel.

With all that said, we're still ahead of a rumored fall 2027 launch, and Apple's plans shift constantly behind closed doors, plus features this ambitious have a habit of slipping a year or two. Under-display Face ID in particular has been "two years away" for about five years now.

title: I’ve never been happier that Apple is bad at AI
content:
Macworld





Does it make sense to say “AI is back in the news” when AI, like an obnoxious diva that everyone is already tired of hearing from, insists on making the news like 50 times a day?
AI, on top of the high dive: “Mom! Mom! Look at me! Mom! Mom! Look how high up I am! MOMMM!”
AI’s mom, not looking up from her magazine: “Yes, honey, I see you. You’re very high up. Sigh.”
It does often feel that we’re seeing AI in its creatively dried up and strung out on drugs and booze period, though. This week it went on another bender.
First up, the midterm elections in the U.S. caused a precipitous drop in the value of AI stocks, as concerns that–GASP!–regulation would add to its already concerning bubble trouble.
Are you saying that the U.S. government can actually regulate industries to prevent them from destroying the environment, ruining people’s communities, and being linked to enough deaths to get a Wikipedia entry detailing them all?
What is this? Europe?!
…concerns about an A.I. backlash are compounding fears of runaway spending and rising debt at tech firms.
New York Times, November 5, 2026
If only someone could have told you that AI didn’t need to be shoved into every single thing imaginable! At least the Macalope is breathing a little easier about the possibility of U.S. taxpayers having to bail out the companies that spent billions on data centers only to find no one wants to pay for a chatbot that plans parties for them.
It still seems like it’s full steam ahead on AI at Apple, though, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman: “Apple CEO Presses Software Chief to Pursue More Ambitious AI Strategy.”
Desiring more and frustrated by what he sees as a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors, Ternus pushed his software chief to accelerate the company’s road map and move quickly beyond merely making necessary improvements to Siri.
Faster, pussycat, code, code! (Federighi is widely considered to be a pussycat.) 

				
					

				
			
If you’d like to receive regular news and updates to your inbox, sign up for our newsletters, including The Macalope and Apple Breakfast, David Price’s weekly, bite-sized roundup of all the latest Apple news and rumors.

Foundry




Gurman also believes Siri enhancements are on the way:
…Siri can now execute more complicated requests and integrate more deeply with third-party software…I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year
Hope it’s not a foreign agent! HEY-YOOO! (There are those who say that this entire column was built around that one joke, and the Macalope is here to say, uh, that is actually 100 percent true.)
Sorry. Too soon, Jensen Huang, currently still CEO of Nvidia? “Nvidia Opens Investigation Into Jensen Huang’s Relationship With Suspected Chinese Spy”
It turns out the poster child for black leather jacket addiction had an affair with a suspected Chinese operative who was funneling information to Beijing. Oops. Furthermore, Huang reportedly worked with her to sell chips to Chinese businesses by carefully circumventing U.S. trade restrictions. Double oops.
The revelation raised troubling possibilities because Mr. Huang is one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. revolution as well as an influential ally of President Trump.
Trump was briefed on the matter this past spring and took quick and decisive action by… let the Macalope just put on the ol’ reading glasses here to read what he did…
Huh. This says “…inviting Huang to travel to China with him and going so far as to call him ‘the Great Jensen Huang’.” That’s weird.
It’s gonna be a little tricky for Huang to word a screenshot-of-Notes announcement that he’s stepping down to “spend more time with my family” when his family probably has very little interest in spending more time with him.
Huang might not have to worry about it, though, because accountability is for the little people!
“The board composition suggests this is… a CEO exercising effective control over the board instead of vice versa,” said Jill Fisch, a professor at The University of Pennsylvania’s Carey Law School…
Semafor, November 9, 2026
How does the Macalope get to be CEO of an AI company? You get a huge compensation deal on the premise of being able to deliver competence and responsible governance, but you can still have all the illicit sexy time and illegal trade deals you want. Sounds sweet.
Well, Huang might be… problematic, but he’s just one bad apple in the world of AI CEOs, right?
“Elon Musk Confronted With List of People He’s Killed, Including Children”
Ooh. Okay, well, two is…
“Inside Sources Say Sam Altman Is a Sociopath”
Okay! Okay. You made your point.
(Who is posting those?!)
The Macalope’s not saying he wouldn’t like Siri to be capable of doing more. He’s just saying that if Apple becomes an AI company, we might not like what it does to John Ternus, based on the behavior we’re seeing here.

AirPlay and Bluetooth. A malicious Bluetooth device could pair without user interaction, and another bug could let a nearby attacker corrupt process memory. Several bugs could allow an attacker to bypass the rate limit on ‌AirPlay‌ pairing code attempts.

title: Best AirPods Black Friday deals 2026: Our picks for Pro, standard AirPods and Max
content:
Macworld






Best Black Friday AirPods deals so far: U.S.
AirPods Pro 3: $199 ($50 off, MSRP $249) – but we’ve previously seen $169




Best Black Friday AirPods deals so far: U.K.
AirPods Pro 3:  £200 (£19 off, RRP £219) – we recommend waiting for a better price




PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 9, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is a great time to buy AirPods, with retailers competing to offer discounts across Apple’s earbuds and over-ear headphones. Previous sales have brought substantial savings on established models, clearance bargains on older generations, and even discounts on newly released AirPods. But the biggest percentage saving doesn’t necessarily mean the best buy: an older pair needs to be sufficiently cheaper than its replacement to justify missing out on newer features.
Last Black Friday, standard AirPods 4 briefly dropped to $69 in the U.S., while the noise-canceling version fell to $99 – an $80 saving. Even the then-new AirPods Pro 3 received a discount of around $30, while older AirPods Pro 2 reached approximately $139 before selling out. AirPods Max were available for around $400, roughly $150 below their regular price. U.K. savings were more modest, with AirPods 4 at £99 and AirPods Pro 2 at £169, although stock frequently ran out.
This year, we’d watch AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2 for meaningful discounts, while remaining AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 stock could bring some of the biggest clearance savings. The recently released AirPods 5 may see smaller reductions, making it especially important to compare their price with discounted Pro models. Below, we explain which AirPods to choose and how the offers compare with previous discounts. For savings on Macs, iPads, Apple Watch and more, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which AirPods should you buy this Black Friday?


AirPods Pro 3 – Our best overall choice

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Pro 3 are especially worth considering if you want strong noise cancellation, a secure in-ear fit, or Apple’s hearing-health features. Their foam-infused ear tips help improve the fit, while an in-ear heart-rate sensor adds another reason to choose them over standard AirPods. Battery life is rated at up to eight hours with noise cancellation enabled.
For most buyers looking for noise-isolating earbuds, these would be our first choice. Older AirPods Pro 2 are worth considering only when the clearance saving is substantial.
U.S. Black Friday price:  Amazon has already slashed $50 off the AirPods Pro 3, but we expect the price to go lower. Hopefully by Black Friday they will hit their all-time-low of $169.
U.K. Black Friday price: In the U.K. there’s £19 off the AirPods Pro 3, but we recommend holding out for a better deal. 






AirPods 5 – Best for buyers who prefer earbuds without silicone tips

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods 5 offer a lower-cost entry point and an open-ear design for people who don’t like silicone-tipped earbuds. They include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, alongside Transparency mode and Adaptive Audio.
Check which charging case you’re buying. The Wireless Charging Case package adds wireless charging, longer battery life, a Find My speaker, and volume adjustment by swiping the stems. It’s our preferred package when the price difference is small.
U.S. Black Friday price: We’ve not seen a discount yet on the AirPods 5.
U.K. Black Friday price:  No savings yet on the AirPods 5.






AirPods Max 2 – Best for over-ear listening

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Max 2 are the option to consider if you specifically want over-ear headphones. The March 2026 update introduced Apple’s H2 chip and improved noise cancellation, while retaining the premium design and a choice of colors.
We find them difficult to recommend at full price, so the size of the discount matters. Compare any offer with previous sale prices rather than judging it solely against Apple’s asking price.
U.S. Black Friday price:  Amazon has the AirPods Max 2 for $449.99, that’s $99 off. They could still go lower though. 
U.K. Black Friday price:  The AirPods Max 2 aren’t currently discounted on the U.K. Amazon store, but hopefully we will see some good savings towards the end of the month. 






Other AirPods – Buy only at a worthwhile clearance price

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 can still be worth considering, but compare them with the discounted prices of their replacements. A large reduction from an older model’s launch price can disguise a small saving over a newer, more capable pair.
Check the exact generation, charging case, condition, and seller before buying. For more help choosing, read our AirPods buying guide.
U.S. Black Friday price:  We aren’t yet seeing any savings we’d recommend.
U.K. Black Friday price:  You can get the AirPods 4 with ANC for £109 at Amazon and John Lewis – that’s only £10 less than AirPods 5, so we’d recommend waiting for that price to go even lower.






Other headphones – Worthy AirPods alternatives

				
					

				
			
Beats




If AirPods aren’t in your budget, Apple also sells a line of Beats headphones and earbuds that offer many of the same features for a lower price, including the popular over-ear Solo 4 and PowerBeats Pro 2. We’ll also track headphone deals in our round-up of the best earbuds for iPhone and best over-ear headphones if you’d like to see deals on other brands.
U.S. Black Friday price:  There is $100 off the Beats Studio Pro and $70 off the Solo 4 at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.
U.K. Black Friday price:  There is £64 off the PowerBeats Pro 2 and £50 off the PowerBeats Fit at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.






Should you buy AirPods now or wait for a better deal?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need AirPods immediately. But the sales now stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer is close to a model’s previous low, it can be worth taking: last year’s best deals frequently sold out, and popular offers could go quickly again.
Previous sale prices provide useful benchmarks. We’ve seen AirPods Pro 3 reach $169, while AirPods Max 2 fell to $399 during June Prime Day. An offer above those prices may still be worth considering, but a reduction from Apple’s regular price doesn’t automatically make it an exceptional deal.
For AirPods 5, waiting for a discount makes sense if you aren’t in a hurry: they didn’t receive a significant reduction during October Prime Day. With AirPods Max 2, we’d hold out for a substantial saving rather than pay full price.
Compare retailers, too. Amazon isn’t always cheapest: Walmart and Best Buy also compete on AirPods pricing, while Argos offered competitive U.K. deals last year. Our guide to the best time to buy AirPods has more advice on purchase timing.






Should you buy an old pair of AirPods? 
Older-generation AirPods can be a good buy at the right clearance price. Compare their actual selling price with the discounted price of their replacement, rather than focusing on the percentage saving from an old launch price. A substantial discount can make an older pair worthwhile; a small difference may leave you sacrificing useful features for little saving.
AirPods 4 are harder to recommend now that AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, starting at the same $129 price previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC. Check which AirPods 4 version you’re buying—there were models with and without noise cancellation—and look for a substantial saving over AirPods 5.
AirPods Pro 2 remain worth considering if they’re significantly cheaper than Pro 3. However, the newer model improves fit, noise cancellation, and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing. Compare their sale prices carefully: a strong Pro 3 discount could make the older pair’s clearance offer less attractive.
The original AirPods Max also need a substantial discount to justify choosing them over Max 2. The newer headphones add the H2 chip, improved noise cancellation, and features including Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. Check the generation rather than relying on the charging port alone: the original AirPods Max were also sold in a USB-C version.
Buying older stock new is different from buying used or refurbished AirPods. For those pairs, check the stated condition, charging case, warranty, and returns policy, and buy from a reputable seller. Be cautious about battery condition and unusually low marketplace prices, since convincing counterfeits can resemble genuine AirPods. Our guide explains how to spot fake AirPods.
For more advice, see our AirPods buying guide and guide to the best time to buy AirPods.






AirPods deals to avoid

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Check exactly what an offer includes before comparing prices. Different charging-case packages can affect features and value, so make sure you’re comparing equivalent versions. Also check any spending requirements, contracts, or rebates attached to offers advertising “free” AirPods.
Judge the price against previous selling prices as well as the advertised discount. A large saving from the recommended retail price doesn’t necessarily mean a particularly good deal if retailers regularly charge less.
Check whether the listing is for a new, refurbished, or used pair. For used or refurbished AirPods, look for clear information about condition, warranty, and returns coverage. Battery condition deserves particular caution: a low purchase price may be less attractive if listening time has deteriorated.
Finally, check who is selling and dispatching your order, particularly when shopping through a marketplace. Unusually low prices from unfamiliar sellers warrant caution, since counterfeit AirPods can look convincing. Our guide explains how to tell if AirPods are fake.






How we choose AirPods deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on AirPods reviews. We consider sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, battery life, and everyday use – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our AirPods Pro 3 review assessed how securely the redesigned ear tips stayed in place during exercise, checked battery life against Apple’s claims, and evaluated the heart-rate sensor. Our AirPods Max 2 review weighed their excellent sound and noise cancellation against drawbacks including weight and the Smart Case.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. Our Best AirPods guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the best choice for everyone: fit, listening habits, and the features you need all matter.

title: Anker Launches Eufy Security Cam With Auto-Tracking Light
content:
Anker today launched the Eufy TrackLight Cam S1, which it says is the world's first outdoor security camera with an auto-tracking light for actively deterring intruders. The TrackLight Cam S1 is compatible with Apple Home when using the Anker HomeBase, so it can be used alongside other smart home devices in a HomeKit setup.

There's a 15,000mAh battery and a 5.5-watt solar panel for continuous operation, and IP65 dust and water resistance offers protection from the elements. There is no built-in storage, and users will need to add a microSD card or connect to the HomeBase. No subscription is required.

title: macOS 27.2.1 Fixes eMudhra Certificate Flaw in Command-Line Tools
content:
The macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 update Apple released today addresses the eMudhra certificate vulnerability, and Apple recommends users update to the latest software.


For Macs that run macOS 26 or macOS 15, Apple has released macOS 26.7.3 and macOS 15.8.3.

blocked the compromised certificates in Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple frameworks in October to protect most users, but command-line tools like curl and git were still able to accept them. With macOS 27.2.1, command-line tools will no longer accept the certificates.

Prior to releasing the macOS 27.2.1 update, Apple offered instructions for those who wanted to protect themselves from the compromised eMudhra certificates when using command-line tools, directing users to manually remove the affected root certificates from their Mac's "/etc/ssl/cert.pem" file.

has those instructions available for users who are unable to update their Macs.

The compromised security certificates were issued by certificate authority eMudhra. An investigation launched by Mozilla found the certificates used private key values below 256, making them trivial to recover. Attackers could use the keys to create fraudulent certificates that appeared valid for any website.

macOS Golden Gate 27.3 beta, but with the fix also included in macOS 27.2.1, users won't need to wait until December for protection.

title: Agentic Siri is coming, and that’s just the beginning
content:
Macworld





Siri AI is just the beginning. According to the latest newsletter from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who is always dialed-in to the inner workings of Apple, the new CEO John Ternus is pushing to make Apple a bigger player in the AI space.
While he had great things to say publicly about Siri AI at the launch of iOS 27, he is apparently delivering a somewhat different message in private. He seems aware, Gurman said, of the fact that Apple’s AI offerings are far behind rivals and not moving ahead with the same urgency. In a closed-door meeting with Craig Federighi, Ternus pushed to accelerate the company’s roadmap and move quickly past the long-overdue improvements to Siri.
With the OS 27.3 updates, developers will finally be able to make their apps accessible to Siri, so that Siri can perform in-app actions and access their data, if desired. Along with on-screen awareness and personal context, it’s the final pillar of the advanced capabilities Apple first announced two years ago.
But the latest trend in AI is agents. What started with hobbyist software like OpenClaw has grown into consumer-ready products like Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet. These AI agents run continuously and somewhat autonomously, taking care of almost anything a person can do online or on their phone or computer. There are some concerns over privacy and safety, and rightfully so, but they have already proven to be very popular.
That is a big step beyond “tell Siri to take actions within apps” and it’s where Ternus would like to take things. Gurman said Apple could make Siri act more like an autonomous agent “as early as next year,” and notes that the company hardly has a choice–announcing such a major feature at WWDC in June would put Apple a year behind the principal players else in the AI space, at least.
Gurman’s report paints the picture of a CEO concerned not just with matching AI companies feature-for-feature, but recognizing the increasing role of AI in computer use in general. The general idea is that, over time, more of what we do on our computing devices will be handled not by typing, clicking, and swiping, but by a personal agent that can essentially use any software we want it to at our direction. If you’re a company like Apple whose strength comes from selling physical computing devices and creating the operating systems that runs on them, ceding that level of control to a rival company could be an existential threat.

title: Apple releases security updates: iOS 27.2.1, 26.7.3, and 18.7.12
content:
Macworld





Apple has released a set of OS updates aimed around security updates. For those on the latest version of iOS, that is iOS 27.2.1. If you haven’t or can’t update to iOS 27, there are updates to older versions that include these critical software updates: iOS 26.7.3 and iOS 18.7.12.
These updates are joined by similar updates for Apple’s other platforms: macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS. 
Apple’s release notes only says, “This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your iPhone.” This is the boilerplate text for security releases. Apple’s security releases page does not list any of these OS updates at the time of this writing. It will likely be updated shortly to enumerate the security vulnerabilities addressed.
As we wrote back in September, frequent operating system releases that fix dozens of security vulnerabilities are the new normal. The latest AI coding tools have gotten so good that they may it much easier to find and exploit security holes, but also much easier to find and fix them. The race is on, and we can expect more updates that fix a much larger number of security flaws to be a regular thing for at least a year or more.

title: macOS 27.3 increases security with changes to Full Disk Access
content:
Macworld





Back in October, Apple announced a major security change to macOS. The change involves Full Disk Access (FDA), a permission that, when granted to an app requesting it, allows that app to access protected sections of macOS, such as data caches, mail, backups, and more.
The change is coming in macOS 27.3, which has recently started its developer beta cycle and should be available as a public beta soon. As itspdfu points out in a post, users will need to make the extra effort to allow an app to have FDA. Users will have to go into System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access and add the app manually. Previously, the app would be able to add itself to the FDA list and the installer would instruct users to simply toggle on FDA for it.


macOS 27.3 starts implementing changes to Full Disk Access (FDA). Here’s what ‘very explicit user action’ may mean.
When an app tries to read a protected file without FDA, macOS doesn’t prompt the user to grant permission. Instead, it automatically denies access and records that… https://t.co/zjUuEh7EIb
— pdfu (@itspdfu) November 7, 2026





The reason for the change: AI. “As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially,” according to Apple in a developer blog post. “We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy.”
Itspdfu also states that macOS 27.3 introduces “‘Private Folders,’ a new folder-by-folder permission configured like Full Disk Access.” However, this feature doesn’t seem to be fully capable as of yet. 
The macOS 27.3 beta 1 for developers was released on November 2. The official release of macOS 27.3 is expected in December.

title: Apple Continues to Say Some AI Features Will Have Fees for Extra Usage
content:
Apple continues to advise customers that certain Apple Intelligence features that rely on its server-side Private Cloud Compute system have daily usage limits, with expanded access to such features to be "available for a fee in the future."


Apple has repeatedly mentioned these upcoming fees in press releases over the past several months, but it has yet to provide any specific details about timing or pricing. The company did confirm that expanded access to the features will eventually be included with select iCloud+ plans, rather than something available for a standalone fee.

Extra server-side usage for a fee will be available for Siri AI, Image Playground, the Extend and Reframe options in the Photos app, shortcuts created with natural language in the Shortcuts app, and more. Apple says daily limits may vary by feature, request complexity, system demand, system policies, and other unspecified factors.

iCloud+ plans and prices in the U.S.:

  
50GB: $0.99/month

  
200GB: $2.99/month

  
2TB: $9.99/month

  
6TB: $29.99/month

  
12TB: $59.99/month

It is unclear if these prices will increase once the expanded AI access is included.

Apple having said that extra usage will be included with "most" iCloud+ plans seemingly rules out the 50GB plan for $0.99 per month receiving this benefit at a minimum.

Logic Pro

Apple last week updated Logic Pro for Mac with a new intelligent assistant feature that can help creators "navigate production workflows, start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project."


The intelligent assistant has a monthly usage limit, with expanded usage packs available to users with an active Apple Creator Studio subscription in the United States, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Mexico, and the United Kingdom. In the U.S., the usage pack is currently priced at $49.99 and valid for one year.

To purchase additional usage, choose Logic Pro from the macOS menu bar, choose Intelligence Features, choose Show Usage, then choose Buy More Usage.

support document, Apple says some intelligence features in Apple Creator Studio apps are powered by "third-party providers." For the Logic Pro assistant, it says the feature is "powered by Google Gemini," so it appears it is not considered to be part of Apple Intelligence and thereby extra usage will not be included in iCloud+ plans.

An external SSD is a straightforward way to expand your Mac’s storage, carry files between devices and keep backups close at hand. Whether you need more room for photos or a fast drive for video projects, our recommendations cover a range of capacities, connections and budgets.
Compared with mechanical hard drives, SSDs generally offer faster transfers in smaller, lighter designs. Most portable models take power directly from your Mac, making them convenient companions for a MacBook. Desktop drives offer another option if your storage will mostly stay in one place.
Choosing the right SSD involves more than finding the highest advertised speed. Your Mac’s ports, the drive’s connection and the supplied cable all affect performance. For everyday backups, capacity and value may matter more than maximum speed; for demanding creative work, faster transfers can justify paying extra.
We compare tested performance, Mac compatibility, portability and value, alongside practical features such as rugged protection, encryption and warranty coverage. Below, you’ll find our top picks for different needs, alternatives worth considering and buying advice to help you choose.
